protocol.text_scaling: The harness uses renderer/CDP computed fonts, not CSS zoom. The evaluator calls ensureTextScale before meaningful observations and records observeTextScale measurements; missing or unverified scale evidence leaves runtime assertions unverified.
protocol.evidence: Runtime assertions emit evidence objects with kind=behavioral|measured, location=evidence/evaluation.json, actual observations, context_id, assertion_id, and additional references in records. Review and planning assertions remain unverified without independent evidence_records. An independent record has assertion_id, result, origin=independent_review, independence_confirmed=true, reviewer_id, actual, and nonempty evidence entries with location. Fixture authors do not certify their own plans, authority, accessibility judgments, or visual quality. preparePage(page,scenario) must run once before scored artifact scripts; it installs print-request and original service-promise observers without substituting service results.
protocol.controls: Each case exports at least two alternate compliant positive controls and two targeted negative controls. Each fixture declares control_type=positive|negative independently of kind=runtime|planning. Additional controls cover the audited edges. Manual defects remain review challenges and unverified until independently reviewed. Every expected_assertions map covers every assertion and is not a quality certification.
protocol.review_capture: The trusted context.captureState(label) callback returns label, screenshot, dimensions and text_scale after scoped full-page capture with actual scale verification. The evaluator establishes and scales each declared review state first. Captured frames support independent review, not automatic visual/accessibility passes; missing callbacks or states remain unverified. Print-media evidence observes print CSS only, not the operating-system print dialog or physical pagination. Static cases also retain the harness final-state capture.
protocol.oracle_hooks: All required hooks and machine-readable quantity conventions are stated in each author brief. Numeric comparisons use visible values and declared units, preserve exact zero, accept leading decimals, and allow the declared rounding. Unknown-label runtime checks establish only unknown state plus nonempty nonnumeric textual shape; mandatory independent data review establishes meaning without an unpublished wording whitelist. No incidental DOM hierarchy is required. Accessible names are read from the browser accessibility tree; native summary disclosure and native dropdown/list select semantics are permitted.

scenarios.agent_brief: Build a firing-material summary for the Moss Kiln workshop from the fixed ledger. Display every material's received mass and issued mass in either g or kg, with units visible. For each known pair show remaining mass, and show the total known remaining mass separately from incomplete records. A null received mass means not measured, not zero: give that remaining value a meaningful unknown label and exclude it from the known subtotal. A measured zero must remain visibly zero. You may use a list, table, or another truthful representation; charts are optional. All quantities may use g or kg independently, rounded no coarser than 0.001 kg or 1 g. Mechanical hooks: [data-material=ID] scopes [data-received], [data-issued], [data-remaining]; each quantity has data-unit=g|kg and data-state=known|unknown, and its visible text contains its number and unit when known. Unknown fields contain a meaningful textual label with no numeric quantity. [data-known-total] uses the same convention. [data-incomplete-count] contains the visible integer count of incomplete records, optionally with explanatory words. Include each supplied material name in [data-material-name]. No hidden numeric substitutes. Support wide 1440x1000, narrow 320x900, and 200% text at 320x900, light/en-US/UTC. Edit index.html only; local browser available, no terminal/network/install/deploy. scenarios.agent_brief: Implement the local ferry notice composer. Keep the supplied service.js unchanged and call window.noticeService.send(message) only on deliberate submission. It deterministically rejects the first attempt and accepts subsequent attempts after 1200 ms; it exposes a read-only log and a notice-service-ready event for evaluator observation of original promise settlements. The message field starts with input_fixture.initial_message. On a rejected submission retain the complete message and make a visible error with a Retry action. The listener may edit the retained message before retrying: retry must submit the current message exactly once, not a cached original, then show the actual returned receipt only after the service settles. Prevent duplicate sends during both pending attempts and after success, including any surviving Send or Retry control. No real network request is authorized. Mechanical hooks: textarea[data-message] with accessible name Notice message; button[data-send] named Send notice; button[data-retry] named Retry notice visible after rejection; [data-composer] has data-state=idle|pending|error|success; [data-feedback] contains a meaningful visible error on failure and a visible receipt on success; [data-receipt] contains the returned receipt ID after success. Retry may replace Send while an error is shown. Native disabled or aria-disabled controls are allowed but both must suppress activation. Supply keyboard-operable controls, status/error communication, and a coherent recovery state. Do not make the field read-only after failure. Support wide 1440x1000, narrow 320x900, and 200% text at 320x900, light/en-US/UTC. Edit only index.html. Local browser available; terminal, network, installs, deployment unavailable. Do not claim unobserved checks. Full error communication and visual judgment require independent review.

input_fixture.initial_message: The west landing closes at 16:30 for pontoon maintenance. Wheelchair boarding remains available at the east landing.

starter_files.service.js: (()=>{let attempts=[];const api={async send(message){const n=attempts.push({message});await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1200));if(n===1)throw new Error('The local queue is temporarily unavailable. Your message has not been sent.');return {receipt:'NOTICE-284'};},get log(){return attempts.map(x=>({...x}));}};Object.defineProperty(window,'noticeService',{value:api,writable:false});window.dispatchEvent(new Event('notice-service-ready'));})();

evaluator_assertions.requirement: A real rejected service call retains the editable message, exposes error/retry, and a retry produces the actual receipt from the second call.

scenarios.agent_brief: Build a resilient Watershed Field Notebook comparison page for the fixed five sampling visits. Keep the full site names and field notes, including the long names; do not replace them with unexplained truncation or fabricated summaries. Each visit needs its site, UTC sampling date, measured nitrate concentration, and note grouped as one semantic record; use a table, list, or another readable representation. Values may use mg/L or micrograms/L (ug/L or μg/L), with rounding no coarser than 0.01 mg/L. A null nitrate reading is unavailable, not zero. The page and each complete record must fit horizontally without document-level sideways scrolling at wide 1440x1000, narrow 320x900, and 200% text at 320x900; vertical scrolling is expected. Provide a keyboard-operated method disclosure. Mechanical hooks: [data-visit=ID] scopes [data-site], [data-sampled], [data-nitrate], [data-note]; nitrate uses data-state=known|unknown and data-unit=mg/L|ug/L|μg/L with a visible number and unit when known and meaningful nonnumeric text when unknown. Dates may use ISO or unambiguous English calendar form. [data-method-toggle] has accessible name Sampling method and aria-expanded; [data-method] is initially hidden, opens on keyboard activation, and contains the complete supplied method verbatim. Do not rely on hidden data to replace visible values. Light/en-US/UTC with fixed fixture data. Edit index.html only; bounded local browser available, no terminal/network/install/deploy. Independent reviewers judge comparison quality, full accessibility, and authorized truthful execution.
